newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea allows currency conversion in special zone.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea allows currency conversion in special zone.

text.p: North Korea will allow its currency to be exchanged directly with U.S. dollars in a bid to boost business in a northeast free-trade zone, a South Korean Finance Ministry official said on Monday.
The official, who asked not to be identified, said the Stalinist country explained it would set the exchange rate at 200 North Korean won per dollar.
The plan was revealed during a Tumen River Area Development Programme meeting in Beijing on May 28.
"The system seemed to be introduced to boost foreign investments in the Rajin-Sonbong zone," the official said.
The free-trade zone was set up in 1991 in the northeast corner of the peninsula which borders Russia and China.
He said the system was to be implemented on June 1, but that no confirmation has been received.
North Korea, sliding into famine, is desperate for hard currency.
Other parts of the communist country would rem,ain under the old system, whereby foreigners exchange hard currency for special units at an official exchange rate of 2.16 North Korean won per dollar.
The black market rate for the special currency is 100 North Korean won per special unit, he added.
